issues.description: Method name mismatch between template Main and the specification/solution: the template's Main calls farm.feed(), but the problem statement UML and the solution use feedAllAnimals(). This inconsistency can confuse students about which method to implement or call and may lead to compilation errors if they follow the Main example.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Main to call farm.feedAllAnimals() instead of farm.feed(), or add a delegating feed() method in Farm that calls feedAllAnimals(), so the example in Main matches the method students are expected to implement.

issues.description: Method signature mismatch in the template Farm: singFarmSongVerse is declared without a parameter (the Animal parameter is commented out), whereas the UML/problem statement and the solution define singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This prevents students from directly implementing the verse printing logic as specified and may confuse them about the intended helper method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the Animal parameter in the template method signature: change private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) so it matches the UML and the solution, enabling students to implement verse printing per-animal.

issues.description: The template Main.java calls farm.feed(), but the problem statement and the solution implementation use the method name feedAllAnimals(). This mismatch can confuse students about which method they are expected to implement on Farm (feed() vs. feedAllAnimals()).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent: update template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to call farm.feedAllAnimals() instead of farm.feed(), or alternatively add a feed() method in the Farm class that delegates to feedAllAnimals(). Prefer using feedAllAnimals() to match the problem description and solution.
